findings.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the sort key. With order_by='-datetime' in the audit logs endpoint, that key is a datetime, so a TypeError is raised. DateTimePaginator avoids this by converting to an epoch timestamp first.

verifier.reason: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key in src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838-840 passes getattr(item, self.key) directly to math.floor/math.ceil, which raises TypeError when OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73-83) uses it with order_by='-datetime' on AuditLogEntry.datetime (a DateTimeField at src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69). In contrast, DateTimePaginator.get_item_key at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:233-236 converts the datetime to a numeric epoch timestamp first.

findings.claim: The enable_advanced check in the audit logs endpoint accesses organization_context.member.has_global_access without a None check. member is None for callers without membership, such as superusers, API keys/org auth tokens, legacy org ApiKeys and internal-integration proxy users, so an AttributeError is raised.

verifier.reason: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 unconditionally evaluates `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` without checking if `organization_context.member` is `None` (it is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None` at src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:346). While `request.user.is_superuser` short-circuits for superusers, non-superuser callers without org membership that pass `OrganizationAuditPermission`—such as legacy org `ApiKey` (src/sentry/api/authentication.py:272), `OrgAuthToken` (src/sentry/api/authentication.py:492), and SentryApp proxy users (src/sentry/auth/access.py:917-918)—hit an `AttributeError` on every GET request.

findings.claim: When enable_advanced_features is true, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result passes a user-supplied negative cursor.offset directly into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing, so a crafted cursor (e.g. 0:-10:0) raises an error that is not converted to BadPaginationError and results in a 500.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877-882, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0 (accepted by Cursor.from_string at src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:51-58), OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result sets start_offset = cursor.offset and slices queryset[start_offset:stop], which raises Django's negative-indexing error on a QuerySet. Neither get_result nor Endpoint.paginate (src/sentry/api/base.py:540-541, which only catches BadPaginationError) catches this error, so it propagates to Endpoint.handle_exception_with_details (src/sentry/api/base.py:328) and returns HTTP 500.
